text:
Ravi: quick idea: instead of hard lanes, introduce 'soft-slot borrowing' (aka grace windows). small virtual allocations that let bursty requests try to complete without touching reserved/burst pools
Sasha: sounds promising. what's the failure mode? could this amplify hot-spot tenants?
Ravi: failure modes: (a) repeated borrow attempts thrash coalescer, (b) wasteful KV populates, (c) headroom accounting confusion. mitigate via limits + decay counters
Eli: propose concrete invariants so we don't drift: 1) soft-slots never preempt reserved or guaranteed capacity, 2) they have both a token cap and a time cap, 3) borrow attempts are rate-limited per-tenant with exponential backoff
Nora: how do we implement without touching coalescer internals? goal is low-touch runtime change
Ravi: shim sits between enqueue and coalesce. flow: enqueue -> borrow-check -> tag request (soft=true) -> coalesce. coalescer treats tagged requests as best-effort and uses an admission weight when forming bundles
Eli: admission weight? explain
Ravi: each request gets a weight vector: reserved=100, steady=50, soft=10. when forming a bundle we prefer higher weights but still allow low-weight items to join if headroom permits. prevents cheap soft requests from starving heavy ones
Sasha: interesting. need to be careful with batching heuristics: if soft requests consistently form smaller micro-batches, we could increase per-token cost
Nora: telemetry needs: borrow_attempts, borrow_success, borrow_evicted, soft_batch_size_hist, soft_to_reserved_fallback, kv_transient_hits
Ravi: agree. also trace samples when soft fallback rate > 5% for a tenant in 1m window
Eli: KV concern: if soft requests prime the KV and then get evicted, we pay twice. option: mark soft-induced KV entries as low-priority (TTL=short) and do not pin them to GPU prefetch queues
Sasha: UX/policy: tenants can be auto-eligible via spike-detection or manually opted-in in tenant config. auto-eligible only after hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping
Nora: what's spike-detection? simple rule or ML?
Ravi: start simple: moving window QPS + percentile latency. rule: enable soft-eligibility after N requests exceed P95 threshold 3x in 30s. disable after 5m calm. config knobs exposed
Eli: code sketch for borrow-check:
```
bool try_borrow(tenant) {
  if (tenant.is_reserved) return false;
  if (!tenant.soft_enabled) return false;
  if (tenant.borrow_count >= config.max_borrows_per_min) return false;
  if (global_soft_usage > config.max_global_soft_pct) return false;
  tenant.borrow_count++;
  return true;
}
```
Sasha: rollout plan? need canaries + metrics gating so we don't regress SLOs
Ravi: canary 10 tenants with known burst patterns -> staging -> gradual prod. gating: no increase in 99th latency for reserved tenants, and soft-cost-per-token within threshold
Nora: also add shield: if evictions spike > X, auto-disable soft globally for 1m
infra-bot: scheduled: batcher/soft-slot-shim alpha -> staging on 2026-04-01T04:00Z :rocket:
Eli: operational nit: make borrow decisions idempotent for retries to avoid double-counting when enqueue sees duplicates
Sasha: agree. also expose per-tenant dashboard showing borrow success/fail, last-eviction, avg soft-batch size
Ravi: next steps: 1) write short RFC with invariants and admission weight semantics, 2) telemetry spec (Nora owns), 3) implement shim + unit tests, 4) small canary run. I'll draft RFC by EOD
Nora: i'll draft telemetry and dashboards. will coordinate with product for opt-in UX
Eli: i'll prototype TTL-for-soft-KV and add trace hooks
Ravi: TL;DR: soft-slot borrowing = low-risk, tunable grace windows to absorb bursts without revamping coalescer. key controls: token+time caps, admission weights, hysteresis, soft-KV TTLs, telemetry + global shield :thumbsup:
